reviews.lessons: The strategy has zero trades, so there is no empirical performance to critique — every observation below is structural, not statistical. The 'any-of' tier now contains six conditions of which virtually any live large-cap will satisfy at least one on any given day (above_50dma alone clears the bar in a bull market), meaning the any-of gate provides almost no filtering power and the 'all' tier is doing all the real work. Lowering phase_confidence to 0.35 and widening ATR/RSI bands simultaneously means the system will now accept weaker Wyckoff reads AND noisier volatility regimes AND more stretched momentum — three loosened filters at once with no new compensating constraint. R:R dropping from 1.6 to 1.3 directly fights the MTF interest drag: at 1.3 the gross target is only ~1.3× the stop, and after ~0.4–0.5% round-trip+interest cost on a 5-day hold the net expected value compresses to near zero unless win-rate is high, which lower-confidence entries will not deliver. With no live trades the parameterisation feels increasingly tuned to generate entries rather than to generate profitable entries.
reviews.changes: 1) Restore R:R minimum to 1.6 — below this the MTF+commission drag makes expectancy negative unless win-rate exceeds ~60%, which low phase_confidence entries will not achieve. 2) Fix the any-of tier: collapse the six conditions to two genuine confirmations — require BOTH volume_confirming > 0.5 AND (above_200dma > 0.5 OR trend_up > 0.5); this forces volume agreement and trend alignment together, not just one of six easy alternatives. 3) Hold phase_confidence at 0.35 provisionally but add a hard floor: if phase_confidence < 0.45 then require wyckoff_phase_score >= 1.0 (not 0.5) — i.e., low-confidence reads must have a clear phase score to compensate. 4) Tighten ATR band back to 1.0–6.0; the 0.7 lower end admits stocks with insufficient daily range to reach targets before interest compounds, and the 8.0 upper end admits gap-and-trap volatility that blows stops. 5) Add a minimum target-distance rule: gross target must be >= 1.8% from entry so that after MTF costs there is still a meaningful net gain even on a 3-4 day hold. 6) Run the revised rules on the last 60 days of historical data across the universe before deploying capital — the desk has never had a live trade and needs at least a back-of-envelope hit-rate estimate before loosening was the right direction.

reviews.lessons: The strategy has zero trades, so there is no execution history to evaluate — no wins, no losses, no hold-time distribution, no interest drag data. WideOpen was created by loosening almost every filter from v3 (phase_confidence, R:R, RSI band, ATR band, trend filter), which raises the theoretical trade frequency but simultaneously increases the risk of entering low-quality setups that lack momentum and bleed to MTF interest over the hold period. The 'any-of' tier now includes six conditions, several of which are redundant or nearly always true (e.g. above_50dma and above_200dma can both be true at once), so the gate is effectively toothless. A minimum R:R of 1.3 with a 1.5% risk budget is borderline — after ~0.45% round-trip + interest cost on a 4-day hold, the net R:R on margined positions is closer to 1.0:1, meaning the strategy needs a win rate above 50% just to break even, and that bar rises every additional day held.
reviews.changes: 1) Restore phase_confidence minimum to 0.42 — entries near 0.35 are speculative and the cost structure punishes speculation. 2) Restore R:R minimum to 1.6; at 1.3 the net expectancy after costs is too thin. 3) Collapse the 'any-of' tier to exactly TWO conditions that must both be satisfied: volume_confirming > 0.5 AND (above_200dma > 0.5 OR trend_up > 0.5) — this forces momentum + trend agreement rather than letting any single soft signal suffice. Remove the redundant above_50dma standalone condition; it can be folded into the trend_up check. 4) Tighten RSI upper bound back to 72; entries above 72 chase extended moves that rarely complete additional 5-10% gains inside 5 sessions. 5) Add an explicit entry staleness rule: if the setup signal is older than 1 session, skip — stale Wyckoff reads in large-caps resolve or fail quickly. 6) Keep all position limits, hold caps, and 1.5% risk sizing exactly as-is. Run for 15–20 trades before any further loosening.

reviews.lessons: Wyckoff_v3_WideOpen has zero trades, so there is no execution history to judge — every parameter relaxation (lower phase_confidence, wider RSI band, looser ATR band, softened trend filter) was made speculatively to increase trade frequency, but we cannot confirm whether those relaxations actually capture good setups or merely lower the bar enough to let marginal ones through. The 'any-of' tier now contains six conditions, at least one of which (above_50dma > 0.5) is trivially true for a large fraction of large-caps in any uptrend, meaning the gate may be nearly open by default. With no closed trades, MTF interest drag, stop tightness, and exit-reason mix are all untestable — the system is a hypothesis, not a tested strategy. The risk parameters (1.5% risk/trade, 5-day max, 70% cap) are structurally sound given MTF economics, but they protect nothing if entries never fire or fire on weak setups.

reviews.lessons: WideOpen has zero trades, so there is no execution record to critique — every parameter change made in v3 is untested hypothesis. The loosening of phase_confidence to 0.35, R:R to 1.3, RSI band to 35-78 and ATR band to 0.7-8.0 simultaneously widens the funnel on every axis at once, which is theoretically more permissive but we have no evidence it actually produces more qualifying setups rather than just noisier ones. The 'any-of' tier now requires only ONE of six very easy conditions (above_50dma alone qualifies), making it functionally no filter at all — nearly any stock in an uptrend on any timeframe will pass. MTF at 0.04%/day means a 5-day hold costs ~0.2% interest plus ~0.2% round-trip, so the 1.3 R:R minimum only survives if the move is clean and fast; at 1.3 R:R there is almost no buffer for a slow grind. With no trade history, we cannot distinguish whether the strategy fails to generate signals, fails to execute them, or has never been run against live data.
reviews.changes: 1) Diagnose the pipeline first: run a backtest or paper scan of the v3 filters against the last 20 trading sessions for the 25-stock universe and count how many setups would have qualified — if zero, the filters are still broken; if many, the live feed or order-routing is the problem. 2) Tighten the 'any-of' tier back to meaningful conditions: require BOTH volume_confirming > 0.5 AND (above_200dma OR above_50dma) to avoid the current rubber-stamp quality. 3) Raise R:R minimum back to 1.5 — at 1.3 the MTF cost nearly eliminates the edge on any hold beyond 3 days. 4) Cap ATR at 5.0% — stocks above that are too volatile for a 1.5% risk-per-trade rule to size decently on Rs 2,00,000 capital. 5) Do not change phase_confidence or RSI band further until at least 10 trades exist to evaluate; premature parameter tuning on zero data is noise-fitting.

reviews.lessons: WideOpen has zero trades, so there is nothing to diagnose from outcomes — no stops, no MAX_HOLD_5D exits, no MTF interest drag to measure. The strategy is brand-new (or freshly reset) and has not yet been exposed to the market. Loosening every filter simultaneously (phase_confidence, R:R, RSI band, ATR band, trend filter) before any live validation means the first batch of trades will be the experiment, with real capital at risk. The 'any-of' tier now includes six conditions of which only one needs to be true, making it nearly impossible to fail entry on that tier alone — this is the structural risk to watch.
reviews.changes: 1) Run paper or sim for at least 10-15 trades before drawing conclusions, but apply the following pre-emptive tightening now. 2) Restore the 'any-of' gate to require at minimum TWO of the six conditions to be true simultaneously — a stock that is volume-confirmed AND above-50DMA is a meaningfully better setup than one that merely clears one soft condition. 3) Raise minimum R:R back to 1.5: at 1.3 a trade that takes 4-5 days to work breaks even after MTF interest and brokerage, so there is no edge. 4) Keep phase_confidence at 0.35 as a cautious experiment, but tag every trade with its phase_confidence value so the first review can stratify wins/losses by confidence tier. 5) Flag any trade where the nearest resistance (target) is less than 1.8% away — at that distance MTF drag consumes too large a fraction of the theoretical gain. 6) After 15 closed trades, rerun this review: if MAX_HOLD_5D exits dominate, the phase reads are still weak and confidence threshold must go back up; if STOP exits dominate, entries are still late or ATR band is too wide.

reviews.lessons: Wyckoff_v3_WideOpen has zero closed trades, so there is no empirical loss pattern to diagnose — no MAX_HOLD_5D bleed, no stop clustering, no MTF interest drag to measure. The successive relaxations from v1 through v3 (phase_confidence cut to 0.35, R:R cut to 1.3, RSI band widened to 35-78, ATR floor dropped to 0.7%, trend filter softened to any-of) are parameter loosening without feedback, which is the classic over-fitting-in-reverse trap: the rules are becoming permissive before we know whether the original rules were the problem. The 'any-of' tier now contains six conditions, any single one of which qualifies an entry — in practice that collapses to 'almost always true', meaning phase_confidence ≥ 0.35 and R:R ≥ 1.3 are the only real gates. An R:R floor of 1.3 is marginal against a 0.4-0.5% round-trip + MTF cost stack; a trade that exactly clears 1.3:1 at entry levels will frequently finish near breakeven after costs even if the technicals were right.
reviews.changes: 1) Do not loosen further until at least 10 closed trades exist — freeze the parameter set at v3 as-is for the next live cycle and log every setup that reaches scoring, including those that fail one gate, so near-miss analysis is possible. 2) Tighten the 'any-of' tier back to a minimum-two-of-six requirement rather than any-one-of-six; otherwise phase_confidence and R:R are doing all the work and the Wyckoff/volume/trend features are decorative. 3) Raise the R:R floor to 1.5 given the documented 0.4-0.5% cost stack — at 1.3 a trade needs to be right and fast just to cover costs, leaving no margin for slippage or a one-day pause. 4) Add a mandatory volume_confirming ≥ 0.6 to the 'all' block rather than the 'any' block; volume confirmation is the core Wyckoff entry trigger and should not be optional. 5) After 10 closed trades return here: if MAX_HOLD_5D exits dominate, raise phase_confidence threshold; if STOP exits dominate, widen stops or cut position size, not the R:R minimum.
